teaser.text: Twilio sells the building blocks that let businesses put messages, calls and email inside their own software. A business sends Twilio an instruction through its application, and Twilio connects that instruction to the phone or email networks that reach the customer.

stock.title: Twilio stock forecast
stock.meta_description: Twilio stock forecast with bear, base and bull scenarios, cash-after-stock-pay drivers, and today’s valuation.
stock.opening: Twilio’s weighted value is $153.85 in October 2029, a −40% return, based on 30% bear, 50% base and 20% bull probabilities. It hinges on whether cash after stock pay grows enough to offset valuation compression.
stock.closing: The full memo also explains Twilio’s business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: Where could Twilio’s shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: The forecast points to substantial downside over all three dates. The probability-weighted price is $108.01 in October 2027, $135.92 in October 2028 and $153.85 in October 2029, equal to returns of negative 58%, negative 47% and negative 40% with dividends included, from today’s $258.29.

blocks.heading: What could go right or wrong for Twilio?

paragraphs.text: Cash after stock pay is the central operating assumption. The base case rises from $320 million in October 2027 to $570 million in October 2028 and $750 million in October 2029. The latest complete annual figure was $345.020 million, while the latest quarter produced $210.733 million after stock pay, versus $352.645 million before stock pay. Twilio also raised its 2026 reported free-cash-flow guidance to $1.135–$1.155 billion, although that figure precedes stock pay. The forecast therefore assumes continued operating leverage, but not a large AI windfall.

The bear case falls to $150 million, then $100 million, before recovering to $230 million. That reflects the negative after-compensation results recorded from 2021 through 2023 and pressure from carrier costs. The bull case reaches $500 million, $950 million and $1.300 billion because software add-ons grew above 25% in Q2 2026 and management targets stock pay at 10% of revenue in 2027.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Twilio really make?

paragraphs.text: Stock compensation changes the economic reading. Twilio added back 600,407 of stock pay in operating cash flow because it was not an immediate cash payment. Deducting it analytically leaves “real free cash flow” of 345,020, or 6.8% of revenue. This is not Twilio’s official measure, but it shows what remains after recognizing the cost borne by owners.

blocks.heading: What does Twilio stock valuation look like today?

paragraphs.text: A P/E, or price-to-earnings ratio, shows how much investors pay for each dollar of profit. At $258.29 a share, Twilio trades at a high multiple of recent and expected earnings. The trailing P/E is 36.0 times; the forward P/E is 38.1 times. But second-quarter earnings included a $5.91-per-share noncash tax benefit. Twilio had tax losses that it now expects to use against future profits, so accounting rules allowed it to reduce a valuation allowance. No customer paid that amount, which means the reported profit was not all created by selling more services.

earnings.title: Twilio earnings: guidance and what to watch
earnings.meta_description: Twilio reports October 29, 2026; guidance is raised, while organic growth, gross profit and cash generation matter most.
earnings.opening: Twilio's next results are October 29, 2026. Twilio should be watched for organic growth, gross-profit growth and cash generation.
earnings.closing: The full Twilio memo also answers questions about Twilio's business, rivals, management and risks.

paragraphs.text: Management guides to 18.0%–18.5% revenue growth in 2026. Organic growth guidance is 13.0%–13.5%. It guides to $1.135–$1.155 billion of non-GAAP operating income and free cash flow. Its longer-term promise is $3 billion of cumulative free cash flow for 2025–2027, with stock compensation at 10% of revenue in 2027.

blocks.heading: Has Twilio kept its past promises?

paragraphs.text: Management made two concrete promises. Segment was targeted to reach break-even adjusted operating income by the second quarter of 2025, and Twilio was targeted to reach GAAP operating profitability by the fourth quarter of 2025. Segment reported US$6.009 million of adjusted operating income in that quarter, while Twilio reached its first GAAP operating profit earlier, in the fourth quarter of 2024.

blocks.heading: What have Twilio's last eight quarters shown?

paragraphs.text: Revenue reached 1,499,089 in June 2026, compared with 1,228,425 a year earlier. Operating income reached 84,546, compared with 36,989 in the prior-year quarter. Gross profit and operating income therefore support a real operating recovery.
The latest quarter therefore combines a credible operating recovery with a one-time tax benefit that makes the headline profit look extraordinary.

blocks.heading: What should Twilio watch in the next results?

paragraphs.text: Twilio will report Q3 results after the market closes on October 29, 2026. Investors should first check whether organic growth supports the annual forecast. They should then compare cash generation with the amount needed in the second half. Finally, they should compare reported growth with organic growth, because a widening gap may indicate more carrier charges rather than stronger customer activity.
